alex: quick heads-up — ran a profiling pass on last night's canary. when KV cache climbs past ~78% of limit, batch assembly CPU jumps and p95 token latency spikes. raising this because it caused a rare OOM in a dense-request mix.

lin: can you paste the logs / numbers?

alex: sure — abstracted extract: 
```
p50=22ms p95=110ms p99=240ms
kv_used_before=45.1GB kv_used_after=48.3GB kv_limit=60GB
batch_assemble_cpu% +42% (thread contention on batcher pool)
kernel_selected=fp16-opt -> fallback path int8-conv triggered for some shards
oom_count=1 (recovered via node restart)
```

sara: that looks like fragmentation + a few very long prefixes that inflate KV footprints. also the fallback kernel path seems to be slower in our setup (surprising).

devin: thinking about a mitigation: introduce a "slot-reserve" admission step in the continuous batcher. idea: estimate KV bytes per request (prefix + avg-kv-per-token histogram), reserve a soft slot when forming batches. if reservation would push kv_used past kv_limit - soft_reserve_bytes, apply a soft-spill: try token-trim on prefixes (drop older cached context), else mark for kernel-fallback (int8) as last resort, else queue/reject.

alex: rough pseudo: 
```
req_kv = estimate_kv(req)
if kv_used + req_kv > kv_limit - soft_reserve:
    if can_trim(req):
        req = trim_prefix(req, bytes_to_free)
    elif kernels.has("int8"):
        mark_fallback_kernel(req, "int8")
    else:
        queue_reject(req, reason="kv_pressure")
else:
    reserve_slot(req_kv)
    add_to_batch(req)
```

lin: how reliable is estimate_kv(req)? we need low-cost estimator. maybe prefix_length * avg_kv_per_token[model, seq_len_bucket] + small fixed overhead. keep the estimator decoupled so it's cheap in hot path.

sara: agree. also propose two watermarks: soft and hard. soft triggers trimming/fallback, hard triggers immediate reject and metric increment. plus per-user sliding cap so a single customer can't hog large prefixes.

devin: fairness piece: allot small guaranteed_headroom for interactive sessions (low-latency flag) so we don't hurt chat clients. rest is best-effort.

alex: observed tradeoffs: kernel-fallback prevented OOMs but increased p95 by ~20ms compared to fp16-opt for that workload — it's acceptable vs crash. trimming prefixes reduced memory but occasionally reduced model quality (we saw a delta in exact-match for a couple eval prompts). need to track quality regressions tied to trimming.

lin: I'll add metrics: kv_estimate_histogram, kv_trim_count, kv_fallback_kernel_count, kv_reject_count, kv_trim_quality_regressions (linked to eval suite).

sara: plan for rollout: A/B test with 10% traffic: slot-reserve + soft-spill vs baseline. monitor p50/p95, oom_count, and eval quality. run for 48h. I'll create dashboard and alert on oom_count>0 or p95 regression >30ms.

devin: will draft RFC for config knobs: soft_reserve_bytes, hard_reject_bytes, per_user_kv_limit, fallback_priority = [trim, kernel, reject], interactive_headroom_bytes. include simple defaults: soft_reserve=8GB, hard_reject=1GB, interactive_headroom=64MB.

alex: thanks. two follow-ups: 1) can we add a fast path estimator in Rust that reads token-length + model id and returns kv_estimate in <1us? 2) ensure the batcher doesn't serialize on reservation — reservation should be an atomic bump on per-node atomics (no global lock).

lin: yep on atomic bump. i'll prototype estimator by EOD.

deploy-bot: canary started: infra/canaries/slot-reserve-softspill-2024-06-05 at 2024-06-05T14:23:00Z (traffic=10%)

sara: great — I'll wire dashboards and the eval hooks. if we see quality regression from trimming we can change fallback_priority to prefer kernel fallback first.

alex: any other objections? :thumbsup:

sara: :thumbsup:

devin: ok, filing RFC and linking this thread.

lin: will post a short PR with estimator and the atomic reserve primitive.
